initial_requirements: Transportation agencies need the next generation of the Pontis Bridge Management System to manage bridge inventories and related improvement projects. Authorized users should be able to find and review bridge and project information, support inspection activities, and work with the data needed for planning and analysis. The system must accommodate different agency users and preserve appropriate control over operational and administrative information.

messages.content: Who are the different types of users who will use the next-generation Pontis Bridge Management System, and what are the main tasks or capabilities each role needs to perform?

We expect a few different user groups. Field inspectors need to find bridge records, review existing data, enter or update inspection findings, and attach notes or photos as needed. Planning and asset management staff need to review bridge and project information, analyze condition and needs, and support prioritization of improvements. Program or project staff need to track improvement projects tied to bridges, while supervisors and administrators need broader oversight, user control, and management of operational settings and sensitive information.

What quality attributes are most important for the next-generation Pontis Bridge Management System—for example, performance, availability, usability, security, data accuracy, scalability, or auditability—and are there any specific expectations or thresholds for them?

The most important ones are security, data accuracy, usability, and availability, because people will rely on the system for operational bridge and inspection work. Performance also matters, especially when users are searching large inventories or running analysis, and it should feel responsive in normal day-to-day use. I don’t have specific thresholds yet, like exact response times or uptime targets, and those would need to be confirmed with the agency.
